title: Magnetic Force and Circular Motion
lead: One formula with a sine in it, and one consequence: because the force is always sideways, a magnetic field bends a charge into a circle without ever changing its speed.

blocks.text: Why the path is a circle

blocks.label: A force that only steers
blocks.html:
Start with a stone on a string. Swing it round your head. The string pulls the stone sideways, towards your hand, never forwards along its path.

What happens to its speed? Nothing. It circles at a constant speed, because a sideways pull can change your direction but never your pace.

A magnetic field does exactly this to a moving charge.

  1. The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity.
  2. A perpendicular force cannot speed anything up or slow it down.
  3. So the charge bends into a circle at constant speed.
Key point

Magnetic fields do NO work. They steer, they never accelerate in the everyday sense, and the kinetic energy stays exactly where it started.

The magnetic force supplies the centripetal force, so qvB = mv2/r, which rearranges to r = mv/(qB) (q the charge, v its speed, B the field in tesla, m the particle MASS in kg, r the radius of the circle).

And because F = qvB sin θ (θ the angle between the velocity and the field), there are two ways to feel no magnetic force at all.

Your turn. Name them both.

Answer: two ways.

1. Stand still
F = qvB sin θ
with v = 0
F = 0

2. Travel along the field
θ = 0, so sin 0 = 0
F = qB x 0
F = 0

A stationary charge in the strongest magnet on earth feels nothing at all.

Say it bluntly

A magnetic field steers. It never speeds anything up.

blocks.label: The constants and the unit
blocks.html:
Two masses appear in every circular-motion question on this paper, and they are handed to you in the question so often that people stop reading them. Learn them anyway, because sometimes they are not.

ParticleMassCharge
Electron9.11 x 10-31 kg-1.602 x 10-19 C
Proton1.67 x 10-27 kg+1.602 x 10-19 C
The relationship worth remembering

A proton is about 1800 times heavier than an electron, and both carry the same size of charge.

So in r = mv/(qB), a proton at the same speed travels a circle roughly 1800 times wider. If a question compares the two, that ratio is usually the whole answer.

And the unit of the field. B is measured in tesla, T. Strictly the tesla is the unit of magnetic flux DENSITY, and that word density matters: it is the field per unit area. In the induction lesson you will meet the weber, which is the unit of the flux ITSELF. Keep them apart from the start, because one exam question turns on exactly that distinction.

blocks.label: The magnetic force formulas
blocks.html:
QuantityFormulaNote
Force on a moving chargeF = qvB sin θMax at 90 degrees, zero at 0
Both fields at onceF = q(E + v x B)The full Lorentz force
Radius of the pathr = mv/(qB)Faster means wider
Cyclotron frequencyf = qB/(2πm)No v in it
PeriodT = 2πm/(qB)No v in it either

What every letter means

SymbolMeaningUnit
FForce on the moving chargenewton, N
qCharge of the particlecoulomb, C
vSpeed of the particlemetre per second, m/s
BMagnetic flux density, what everyone calls the magnetic fieldtesla, T
EELECTRIC field, present only in the full Lorentz forceN/C
θAngle between the velocity and the fielddegrees
rRadius of the circular pathmetre, m
mMASS of the particlekilogram, kg
fCyclotron frequency, revolutions per secondhertz, Hz
TPeriod, seconds for one full circlesecond, s
The full Lorentz force, read plainly

F = q(E + v x B)
Two forces added, and they behave completely differently.
The qE part acts whether the charge is moving or not, and pushes ALONG the field.
The qv x B part acts only when it moves, and pushes ACROSS both the velocity and the field.

When a question gives only a magnetic field, the E term is zero and you are back to F = qvB sin θ.

blocks.label: Radius, period and frequency: only one of them cares about speed
blocks.html:
Three formulas describe the same circle, and the difference between them is the point of the whole topic.

QuantityFormulaDoes v appear?
Radiusr = mv/(qB)Yes. Faster means wider
PeriodT = 2πm/(qB)No
Frequencyf = qB/(2πm)No
Key point, and it sounds impossible until you see it

Speed up the particle and it travels a wider circle, but takes exactly the same time to go round.

Why? Because it has further to travel AND it is travelling faster, and the two effects cancel exactly.

Definitions, since the exam asks for them in words. The cyclotron frequency is the number of revolutions per second of a charge in a magnetic field, and it is independent of speed. The period is the time for one revolution, and it is independent of speed for the same reason.

Why it matters, in one machine. This is what makes a cyclotron work. Particles are pushed a little harder each lap; they spiral outward into wider and wider circles; but they keep arriving back at the accelerating gap at exactly the same instants. So the machine can be driven at ONE fixed frequency from start to finish, and it never has to be retuned. Hospitals use cyclotrons to make the isotopes for medical scans.

f and T are the same fact upside down: f = 1/T. Look at the two formulas and you can see the 2πm and the qB simply swap places.

Your turn. An electron circles at 4 x 106 m/s. You double its speed. What happens to the radius, and what happens to the frequency?

Radius
r = mv/(qB)
v doubles, so r DOUBLES

Frequency
f = qB/(2πm)
no v anywhere in it
so f is UNCHANGED

Twice as far round, twice as fast, same time per lap. That is the cyclotron principle in one line.

blocks.label: Entering at an angle: the helix
blocks.tag: cosine gives the pitch, sine gives the radius
blocks.html:
So far the charge entered perpendicular to the field, and went round a circle. What if it enters at some other angle?

Split the velocity into two parts and treat each separately.

ComponentSizeWhat the field does to itResult
Across the fieldv sin θBends itA circle, radius r = m(v sin θ)/(qB)
Along the fieldv cos θNothing, since sin 0 = 0Steady drift straight down the field

Circle plus steady drift gives a helix: a spiral, like the thread of a screw or a stretched spring.

The pitch is how far it advances along the field in one full turn:

p = v cos θ × T (p the pitch in metres, v cos θ the along-field speed, T the period, which does not depend on speed at all)

The hook

Sine gives the radius. Cosine gives the pitch.
Across the field bends, so that is the SINE component and it sets how wide the spiral is.
Along the field is untouched, so that is the COSINE component and it sets how far the spiral advances.

The everyday picture: charged particles from the sun spiral down the earth's magnetic field lines exactly like this, tight circles drifting steadily along the field, until they crash into the atmosphere near the poles and make the aurora.

Your turn. A charge enters at 30 degrees to the field. Which is bigger, its along-field drift or its across-field circling?

The drift.

cos 30 = 0.866, the along part
sin 30 = 0.500, the across part

At 30 degrees it is mostly travelling ALONG the field, so it makes a long, stretched-out helix with a small radius and a large pitch. At 60 degrees the two swap over.

blocks.label: Read the angle before you reach for the sine
blocks.html:
Test 2 uses two different angles in two consecutive skills, and the sines are not interchangeable.

  • Question 2 gives 60 degrees, and sin 60 = 0.866.
  • Question 7 gives 30 degrees, and sin 30 = 0.5 exactly.

Dropping the sine altogether in question 2 gives 1.0 x 106, which is NOT among the options, so the examiner has deliberately made the sine the marked step.

blocks.label: Test 2 question 2, worked in full
blocks.problem: A proton experiences a magnetic force of 3.2 x 10<sup>-14</sup> N while moving through a magnetic field of 0.2 T. The angle between the velocity and the field is 60 degrees. Calculate the speed. Take q = 1.6 x 10<sup>-19</sup> C.
blocks.working:
Given
F = 3.2 x 10-14 N
B = 0.2 T
θ = 60 degrees, so sin θ = 0.866
q = 1.6 x 10-19 C
v = ?

Formula, rearranged in symbols first
F = qvB sin θ
v = F / (qB sin θ)

Denominator first, keeping the powers of ten separate
qB sin θ = 1.6 x 10-19 x 0.2 x 0.866
  = 1.6 x 0.2 x 0.866 x 10-19
  = 0.2771 x 10-19
  = 2.771 x 10-20

Divide
v = 3.2 x 10-14 / 2.771 x 10-20
  = 1.155 x 106 m/s
blocks.redo: Redo it at 30 degrees instead. sin 30 = 0.5, so the denominator falls and the speed rises to 2.0 x 10<sup>6</sup> m/s. Redo it again at 90 degrees: sin 90 = 1, giving 1.0 x 10<sup>6</sup> m/s, which is the answer you would wrongly get by forgetting the sine.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.question:
An electron (9.1 x 10-31 kg, 1.6 x 10-19 C) enters a 0.03 T field perpendicularly at 4 x 106 m/s. Find the radius of its path.

Then: if it entered twice as fast, what would happen to the TIME for one revolution?
blocks.answer:
Given
m = 9.1 x 10-31 kg
v = 4 x 106 m/s
q = 1.6 x 10-19 C
B = 0.03 T

Formula
r = mv / (qB)

Top line
9.1 x 10-31 x 4 x 106 = 3.64 x 10-24

Bottom line
1.6 x 10-19 x 0.03 = 4.8 x 10-21

Divide
r = 3.64 x 10-24 / 4.8 x 10-21

Answer
r = 7.58 x 10-4 m

Every option in this one is 7.58 with a different exponent, so it is purely a powers-of-ten question wearing a physics costume. That is Test 2 question 8.

The time for one revolution would not change at all. T = 2πm/(qB) has no v in it. The circle widens, the speed rises, and the lap time stays put.

blocks.big: Magnetic fields steer, they never speed up
blocks.sub: The radius cares about speed. The period and frequency do not.

title: Force on a Wire, Magnetic Moment and Torque
lead: A wire is just a lot of moving charges, so the same formula applies with the charges bundled together. Bend the wire into a loop and you have built a motor.

blocks.text: From one charge to a whole wire

blocks.label: A wire is a bundle of moving charges
blocks.html:
You already know a single moving charge feels F = qvB sin θ. A current-carrying wire is nothing more than a great many charges moving together, so it feels the sum of all their forces.

Bundle them up and the formula becomes:

F = BIL sin θ

SymbolMeaningUnit
FForce on the wirenewton, N
BMagnetic flux densitytesla, T
ICurrent in the wire, replacing the moving chargeampere, A
LLength of wire actually sitting IN the fieldmetre, m
θAngle between the WIRE and the fielddegrees
Key point, and it is the same sentence as before

Maximum at 90 degrees, where sin 90 = 1 and the wire lies straight across the field.
Zero at 0 degrees, where the wire lies ALONG the field, exactly as a single charge travelling along the field feels nothing.

Only the component ACROSS the field is deflected. One charge or a wire full of them, the rule does not change.

The everyday case: a loudspeaker. A coil sits in a permanent magnet's field, the music signal drives a changing current through it, and F = BIL pushes the cone in and out. Every sound you have ever heard from a speaker is this formula.

Your turn. A 0.5 m wire carries 3 A across a 0.4 T field at right angles. Find the force. Then say what happens if the wire is turned to lie along the field.

At right angles
F = BIL sin 90
F = 0.4 x 3 x 0.5 x 1
F = 0.6 N

Along the field
θ = 0, sin 0 = 0
F = 0 N

Same wire, same current, same field, and no force at all. The angle is doing all the work.

blocks.label: The loop, its moment, and the motor
blocks.html:
Now bend the wire into a loop and put it in a field. One side of the loop is pushed up, the other side is pushed down, and the loop twists.

Two formulas describe it.

QuantityFormulaNote
Magnetic dipole momentm = NIAHow strong a magnet the loop is
Torque on the loopτ = mB sin θ = NIAB sin θZero when aligned

What every letter means

SymbolMeaningUnit
mMAGNETIC MOMENT of the loop. Not a massampere square metre, A m2
NNumber of turns in the coilnone, it is a count
ICurrent in the coilampere, A
AArea the loop ENCLOSESsquare metre, m2
τTorque, the twisting effectnewton metre, N m
θAngle between the loop's moment m and the field Bdegrees
m does two completely different jobs in this course

In r = mv/(qB) and f = qB/(2πm), m is the particle's MASS in kilograms.
In m = NIA and τ = mB sin θ, m is the MAGNETIC MOMENT in A m2.

Read which quantity the question is about before you decide which m you are looking at. Nothing else distinguishes them.

You have already met this behaviour. The electric dipole obeyed τ = pE sin θ, and a compass needle swings to north and stops. The current loop obeys τ = mB sin θ, and does exactly the same thing: it twists until its moment lines up with the field, and then feels no torque at all.

That is a motor, and also the reason a motor needs a commutator. Left alone, the loop would swing to alignment and stop dead. So a real motor reverses the current every half turn, which flips the loop's moment and keeps it chasing an alignment it never reaches. The twisting never stops, and the shaft goes round.

blocks.label: The torque question, worked in full
blocks.problem: A rectangular loop feels a torque of 4.8 x 10<sup>-3</sup> N m in a 0.6 T field, at 30 degrees. Find the magnetic dipole moment. Then, if the loop has 50 turns each enclosing 4 x 10<sup>-4</sup> m<sup>2</sup>, find the current.
blocks.working:
Given
τ = 4.8 x 10-3 N m
B = 0.6 T
θ = 30 degrees, so sin 30 = 0.5 exactly

Step 1: rearrange BEFORE substituting

τ = mB sin θ   so   m = τ / (B sin θ)

Step 2: the denominator on its own

B sin θ = 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.3

Step 3: divide

m = 4.8 x 10-3 / 0.3 = 1.6 x 10-2 A m2

A m2, not kilograms. This m is a magnetic moment.

Step 4: now the current, from the loop's construction

m = NIA   so   I = m / (NA)
  • N = 50 turns
  • A = 4 x 10-4 m2
  • NA = 50 x 4 x 10-4 = 2 x 10-2
I = 1.6 x 10-2 / 2 x 10-2 = 0.8 A

Step 5: check

Both answers are ordinary sizes: a small moment and a modest current. Nothing is off by a power of ten, and the units came out right, which is step 7 doing its job.
blocks.answer: m = 1.6 x 10<sup>-2</sup> A m<sup>2</sup>, and I = 0.8 A
blocks.redo: Redo the first part at 90 degrees. sin 90 = 1, so the denominator doubles to 0.6 and the moment halves to 8 x 10<sup>-3</sup> A m<sup>2</sup>. A loop lying square across the field needs only half the moment to feel the same twist, because that is where the field grips hardest.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.question:
(1) A 2 m wire carries 5 A at 30 degrees to a 0.8 T field. Find the force.

(2) A coil of 100 turns, area 2 x 10-3 m2, carries 0.5 A. Find its magnetic moment.

(3) At what angle does a current loop feel NO torque, and is that position stable?
blocks.answer:
(1) F = BIL sin θ = 0.8 x 5 x 2 x sin 30 = 0.8 x 5 x 2 x 0.5 = 4 N.

(2) m = NIA = 100 x 0.5 x 2 x 10-3 = 0.1 A m2. All three simply multiply.

(3) At 0 degrees, with the loop's moment lying ALONG the field, since sin 0 = 0. And yes, that one is stable: it is the position the field has been twisting it towards all along, exactly like a compass needle settling on north.

blocks.tag: topic 7, as the examiner set it

blocks.big: F = BIL sin theta, maximum across the field
blocks.sub: And m is a mass in the radius formula but a moment in the torque formula.

title: Biot-Savart, Ampere, Wires, Loops and Solenoids
lead: Four arrangements, four formulas, and one unit trap that catches almost everybody: the solenoid counts turns per metre while the toroid counts turns.

blocks.label: The two ways to find a field, and when to use each
blocks.html:
Every magnetic field in this course comes from a current. There are two tools for working out the field, and choosing between them is the first decision in any question.

ToolStatementUse it when
Biot-Savart lawdB = (µ0/4π) x (I dl x r̂) / r2Always true, but laborious. Chop the wire into pieces, find each piece's contribution, add them all up
Ampere's lawThe closed integral of B dot dl equals µ0 IenclosedOnly when the arrangement is SYMMETRIC, and then it is one line

What the letters mean

SymbolMeaningUnit
µ0Permeability of free space4π x 10-7 H m-1
ICurrent in the conductorampere, A
dlA tiny piece of the wire, with a direction along the currentmetre, m
rDistance from that piece to the point you are asking aboutmetre, m
IenclosedCurrent passing THROUGH the loop you drewampere, A
The pairing worth seeing

Biot-Savart is the magnetic Coulomb's law. Both fall as 1 over r squared from a single small source, and both must be summed piece by piece for anything bigger.
Ampere's law is the magnetic Gauss's law. Both are always true, both are only USEFUL when there is symmetry, and both work by drawing an imaginary path or surface.

That imaginary path has a name: an Amperian loop is an imaginary closed path chosen to make Ampere's law easy. Exactly like the Gaussian surface, nothing is built, and you pick it so that B is constant along it.

Your turn. Test 2 asks: Ampere's law is most useful for conductors with high what?

Symmetry.

The law is always true
but only SOLVABLE when you can pick a loop
on which B is constant and along the path

A straight wire, a solenoid and a toroid all have that. A bent piece of wire of no particular shape does not, and for that you are back to Biot-Savart.

blocks.label: The four field formulas
blocks.html:
ArrangementFieldTell it apart by
Long straight wireB = µ0I/(2πr)Falls as 1/r. Has a π
Centre of a loopB = µ0NI/(2R)No π in the denominator
Solenoid, insideB = µ0nINo r at all. n is turns PER METRE
ToroidB = µ0NI/(2πr)N is the TOTAL turns

What every letter means

SymbolMeaningUnit
BMagnetic flux density produced by the currenttesla, T
µ0Permeability of free space4π x 10-7 H m-1
ICurrent in the conductorampere, A
rDistance from the wire, or the radius of the toroid ringmetre, m
RRadius of the current loop itselfmetre, m
NTOTAL number of turnsnone, it is a count
nTurns PER METRE, that is N divided by the lengthper metre, m-1
How to tell the three lookalikes apart in one glance

Wire: 2πr on the bottom, no N.
Loop: 2R on the bottom, and no π anywhere.
Toroid: 2πr on the bottom AND an N on top.

The missing π is the fastest way to spot the loop formula on an option list.

Leave µ0 as 4π x 10-7. The π usually cancels against the π in the formula, which is faster and safer than multiplying it out to 1.2566 x 10-6.

blocks.label: The solenoid and the toroid
blocks.tag: a coil, and a coil bent into a ring
blocks.html:
Two definitions the exam asks for directly.

WordDefinitionIts field
SolenoidA long coil of wireUniform inside, and it counts turns per metre
ToroidA solenoid bent into a ringConfined inside the ring, and it counts TOTAL turns
Why a toroid is used at all

Closing the coil into a doughnut traps the field entirely within the ring. There is almost no stray field outside it.

So where a solenoid would interfere with everything nearby, a toroid keeps itself to itself. That is why toroidal cores are chosen in transformers and power supplies where interference matters.

The everyday case for the solenoid: the door lock in a car, the valve in a washing machine, the starter relay under a car bonnet. Pass a current, get a uniform field inside, and a steel core is dragged into it. That is all a solenoid actuator is.

Your turn. A solenoid is 0.5 m long with 1500 turns. What value of n goes into B = µ0nI?

Formula
n = N/L
Substitute
n = 1500 / 0.5
Answer
n = 3000 per metre

Note it went UP, not down. Dividing by a number less than one makes it larger, and 1500 is offered as a trap answer.

blocks.label: n is turns per metre, N is total turns
blocks.tag: the biggest trap in this topic
blocks.html:
Test 2 question 9: a solenoid 0.4 m long with 800 turns produces 2.5 x 10-4 T. Find the current.

Put 800 into B = µ0nI and you get the wrong answer, and it is one of the offered options.

n = N/L = 800/0.4 = 2000 turns per metre.

Then I = B/(µ0n) = 2.5 x 10-4 / (4π x 10-7 x 2000) = 2.5 x 10-4 / 2.513 x 10-3 = 0.1 A.

The toroid formula uses total turns, the solenoid formula uses turns per metre. That inconsistency is deliberate on the examiner's part, and the defence is to read WHICH symbol the formula carries before you substitute anything.

blocks.label: Test 2 question 14, and why to keep the pi
blocks.problem: At a distance of 5 cm from a long straight wire, the magnetic field is 4.0 x 10<sup>-5</sup> T. Calculate the current. Use µ<sub>0</sub> = 4π x 10<sup>-7</sup>.
blocks.working:
Given
r = 5 cm = 0.05 m
B = 4.0 x 10-5 T
µ0 = 4π x 10-7

Formula, rearranged first
B = µ0I/(2πr)
I = 2πrB / µ0

Substitute, and notice the π
I = (2π x 0.05 x 4 x 10-5) / (4π x 10-7)

The π cancels top and bottom
I = (2 x 0.05 x 4 x 10-5) / (4 x 10-7)
  = (0.4 x 10-5) / (4 x 10-7)
  = (4 x 10-6) / (4 x 10-7)
  = 10 A
blocks.answer: I = 10 A
blocks.redo: If you had turned µ<sub>0</sub> into 1.2566 x 10<sup>-6</sup> first, you would have reached the same answer with four times the arithmetic and four times the chance of slipping. Redo it at r = 10 cm and confirm the current doubles to 20 A, because B falls as 1/r.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.question:
(1) Which of the four field formulas has no π in it, and what does that identify?

(2) Ampere's law needs what property of the arrangement?

(3) A solenoid has 600 turns over 0.2 m. What is n?

(4) According to Biot-Savart, the field around a current element falls off with what?
blocks.answer:
(1) B = µ0NI/(2R), the field at the centre of a loop. No π in the denominator, which is the fastest way to spot it.

(2) Symmetry. The law is always true but only solvable when you can find a loop on which B is constant.

(3) n = N/L = 600/0.2 = 3000 per metre. Again it goes UP.

(4) The square of the distance, 1/r2, exactly like Coulomb's law. Do not confuse it with the whole straight wire, which falls as 1/r because it sums every element along an infinite line.

blocks.label: Every test question on the sources of a magnetic field
blocks.tag: topic 8, as the examiner set it

blocks.sub: The toroid counts total turns, and the loop formula has no pi.

title: Flux, Faraday, Lenz and Inductance
lead: A steady magnetic field, however strong, produces nothing at all. Everything in this lesson follows from that one sentence, and so does every generator ever built.

blocks.text: Induction: change is the whole word

blocks.label: Why a steady field induces nothing
blocks.html:
Start with a bicycle dynamo. Freewheel and the lamp dies. Pedal and it lights. The magnet is just as strong either way, so what is the lamp actually responding to?

Motion. Or more precisely, change.

emf = -N dΦ/dt (emf in volts, N the number of turns, Φ the magnetic flux in webers, and dΦ/dt the RATE at which that flux is changing)

  1. Read the dΦ/dt. It is a rate of change, not an amount.
  2. Park a coil inside the strongest steady magnet you can find and it generates nothing.
  3. Move it, turn it, or switch the field off, and it generates.
Key point

CHANGE is the whole word. A steady flux, however large, induces nothing. This is why a generator has to spin, and why a transformer cannot run on DC.

First, what flux is, and its unit.

Φ = BA cos θ (Φ the magnetic flux in webers, B the flux density in tesla, A the area in m2, θ measured from the normal, exactly as in electric flux)

QuantitySymbolUnitMeans
Flux DENSITYBtesla, THow concentrated the field is
FLUXΦweber, WbThe total, that is B times the area

So one weber is one tesla square metre, read straight off Φ = BA. And Faraday's law is about the flux changing, not the field, which is a distinction Test 2 question 11 turns on directly.

Flux is Φ = BA cos θ, so there are three different ways to change it.

Your turn. Name all three before reading on.

Answer: three ways.

Flux
Φ = BA cos θ
1. Change B
the field strength
2. Change A
the area the loop encloses
3. Change θ
rotate the loop

The third is how a real generator works, and it is why a coil spinning in a perfectly steady field still produces electricity.

Say it bluntly

No change, no emf. The FLUX is what has to change, not the field.

blocks.label: Lenz's law, and why the minus sign is there
blocks.html:
Every induction formula in this course carries a minus sign, and it is always the same law wearing the same coat.

Lenz's law

The induced effect OPPOSES the change that caused it.
That is what the minus sign in emf = -N dΦ/dt means, and what the minus sign in the self-induced emf = -L dI/dt means.

Why it must be so, in one argument. Suppose the induced effect REINFORCED the change instead of opposing it. Then the smallest nudge would strengthen itself, which would strengthen itself again, growing without limit and producing energy from nothing. That is impossible, so nature has no choice: it opposes. Lenz's law is conservation of energy in disguise.

The everyday case you can feel. Push a magnet towards a copper ring and you feel resistance, as though the ring were pushing back. It is. The induced current in the ring makes its own field that opposes your approach. Drop a strong magnet down a copper pipe and it falls in slow motion, as though through treacle, for exactly this reason. The work you do against that opposition is precisely the electrical energy that appears in the ring.

The self-induced emf is the same law applied to a coil opposing changes in its OWN current:

emf = -L dI/dt (L the inductance in henries, dI/dt the rate at which the current is changing in A/s)

Which is why a large inductor resists being switched on quickly, and why switching one off can produce a dangerous spike: dI/dt is enormous for that instant.

blocks.label: The induction formulas
blocks.html:
QuantityFormulaNote
Magnetic fluxΦ = BA cos θIn webers
Faraday's lawemf = -N dΦ/dtRATE of change
Motional emfemf = BLvThree quantities, all multiplied
Self-induced emfemf = -L dI/dtThe minus is Lenz again
Energy in an inductorW = ½LI2The CURRENT is squared

What every letter means

SymbolMeaningUnit
ΦMagnetic flux, the total field through the loopweber, Wb, which is one T m2
BMagnetic flux densitytesla, T
AArea of the loopsquare metre, m2
NNumber of turns in the coilnone, it is a count
LIn BLv, the LENGTH of the moving rod in metres. In the last two rows, the INDUCTANCE in henriesmetre, or henry, H
vSpeed of the moving conductormetre per second, m/s
ICurrent through the inductorampere, A
WEnergy stored in the inductor's magnetic fieldjoule, J
L does two jobs, exactly as m did

In emf = BLv, L is a LENGTH in metres.
In emf = -L dI/dt and W = ½LI2, L is the INDUCTANCE in henries.

Read the formula, not the letter. This course reuses letters constantly and the only defence is knowing which quantity the question is about.

Motional emf is Faraday's law in disguise. A rod of length L sliding at speed v sweeps out area at a rate Lv, so the flux through the circuit changes at a rate BLv, and that rate IS the emf. Nothing new is being claimed.

blocks.label: Eddy currents
blocks.html:
Faraday's law does not care whether anybody meant to build a circuit. Any conducting loop will do, including loops nobody deliberately made.

Definition

An eddy current is a loop of current induced inside a solid conductor by changing flux. A solid block of metal is full of possible loops, so a changing field sets currents swirling inside it, like eddies in a river.

They matter in two opposite ways.

When they are a nuisanceWhen they are the point
In a transformer core they waste energy as heatAn induction hob heats the pan itself and not the surface
Fix: build the core from thin insulated sheets, which breaks up the loops the eddies would takeEddy-current brakes stop a train with no pads to wear out

That fix has a name: the core is laminated. Slice the block into thin sheets, insulate each from the next, and the wide circular paths the eddies wanted are simply not available any more. It is why an opened transformer looks like a stack of thin plates rather than a solid lump of iron.

Your turn. Why does an induction hob heat a steel pan but not your hand?

Because your hand is a poor conductor.

the changing field induces eddy currents
in anything CONDUCTING placed on it
steel conducts, so the currents flow and it heats
flesh barely conducts, so almost nothing flows

Same field, same law, entirely different result, and it is decided by the conductor-or-insulator distinction from the very first lesson of Part B.

blocks.label: Working with induction
blocks.howto: Work each step before sliding down.

frames.teach: Energy stored in an inductor is W = half L I squared. It mirrors half C V squared for a capacitor, and the half is there for the same reason: the current climbed from zero.
frames.ask: Test 2 question 1: a 2 H inductor carries 5 A. Find the stored energy.

frames.check: W = half x 2 x 5 squared = 1 x 25 = 25 J. The current is SQUARED, the inductance is not.
frames.teach: The trap answer is 10 J, which is simply L times I, forgetting both the half and the square.
frames.ask: A rod 0.25 m long moves at 4 m/s across a 0.2 T field, cutting the lines squarely. Find the induced emf.

frames.check: emf = BLv = 0.2 x 0.25 x 4 = 0.2 V. All three simply multiply, with no squares and no constants.
frames.teach: Park the rod and v is zero, so the emf is zero. Faraday again: standing still through the strongest field on earth induces nothing.
frames.ask: A coil sits in a strong but perfectly steady magnetic field. What emf is induced?

frames.check: None at all. d-phi by d-t is zero, so the emf is zero, however strong the field is.
frames.teach: Every induction question on this paper comes back to that one sentence: change is the whole word.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.tag: two conceptual gaps and a unit
blocks.question:
(1) A changing magnetic ______ induces an emf. Which word, and why not the other one?

(2) Which law is the minus sign in emf = -L dI/dt, and what deeper principle is it?

(3) What is a weber, in terms of the tesla?
blocks.answer:
(1) FLUX, not field. Flux is Φ = BA cos θ, so rotating a loop in a perfectly steady field still changes the flux and still induces an emf. Saying field would miss that case entirely, and it is exactly the case a generator uses.

(2) Lenz's law: the induced effect opposes the change that caused it. Deeper down it is conservation of energy, because an effect that reinforced its own cause would make energy from nothing.

(3) One weber is one tesla square metre. The tesla measures flux DENSITY, the weber measures FLUX.

blocks.sub: The flux has to change, and the minus sign is nature fighting back.

kick: Two marks, and a free elimination
title: Transformers and Why They Need AC
lead: A transformer trades voltage for current, and deciding step-up or step-down before any arithmetic eliminates most of the options.

blocks.label: How a transformer works, and why DC kills it
blocks.html:
A transformer is two coils coupled by mutual induction. They are not connected electrically at all. The only thing passing between them is a changing magnetic flux, usually guided by an iron core.

  1. An alternating current in the primary makes a constantly changing flux.
  2. That changing flux threads the secondary.
  3. By Faraday's law, a changing flux through the secondary induces an emf in it.
  4. More turns on the secondary means more flux linkages, so more voltage.

Vs/Vp = Ns/Np

SymbolMeaningUnit
Vp, VsVoltage across the primary and the secondaryvolt, V
Np, NsNumber of turns on the primary and the secondarynone, they are counts
Key point, and it follows from step 1

A transformer works on AC only.
A steady direct current makes a steady flux, and a steady flux induces nothing at all. Connect a transformer to a battery and the secondary gives you one brief pulse as you connect, one as you disconnect, and nothing in between.

The turns ratio is the voltage ratio. Decide the DIRECTION before you calculate anything:

  • More turns on the secondary than the primary, so Ns greater than Np: it steps UP.
  • Fewer turns on the secondary: it steps DOWN.

That single decision usually kills three of the five options on the paper before any arithmetic.

The everyday case: the national grid steps voltage UP to hundreds of kilovolts to carry power across the country, because high voltage means low current and low current means little heat wasted in the cables. Then it steps it back DOWN outside your street. The whole grid runs on AC for exactly this reason, and that is not an accident of history.

Your turn. Np = 100, Ns = 1000, Vp = 240 V. Step up or down, and what is Vs?

Direction first
Ns is greater than Np
so it steps UP
the answer must exceed 240 V

Formula
Vs = Vp x Ns/Np
Substitute
Vs = 240 x 1000/100
Vs = 240 x 10
Answer
Vs = 2400 V

Any option below 240 was eliminated before you touched the numbers.

blocks.label: Test 2 question 6, the efficiency one
blocks.problem: A 240 V transformer lights eight 12 V, 24 W lamps and draws 1 A in the primary. Find the efficiency.
blocks.working:
Step 1: what is the OUTPUT power?

Each lamp is rated 24 W, and there are eight of them.

Pout = 8 x 24 = 192 W

The 12 V rating is not needed. The wattage already tells you the power each lamp uses; quoting the voltage as well is the examiner giving you a spare number to see if you use it wrongly.

Step 2: what is the INPUT power?

Pin = Vp x Ip = 240 x 1 = 240 W

Step 3: efficiency is always output over input

Efficiency = Pout/Pin = 192/240 = 0.8 = 80 per cent

Step 4: check

An efficiency must be below 100 per cent. If you had divided the other way you would have got 125 per cent, which would mean the transformer created energy. That check alone identifies the slip.
blocks.answer: 80 per cent
blocks.redo: Redo it with the primary drawing 1.2 A instead. Input becomes 288 W, so the efficiency falls to 192/288 = 66.7 per cent. More current drawn for the same useful output means more of it is being wasted as heat in the core and the windings.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.question:
(1) A transformer has 500 primary turns and 100 secondary turns, with 240 V in. Step up or down, and what comes out?

(2) What IS a transformer, in one sentence?

(3) Why can it not run on DC?
blocks.answer:
(1) Fewer secondary turns, so it steps DOWN and the answer must be below 240 V. Vs = 240 x 100/500 = 240/5 = 48 V.

(2) Two coils coupled by mutual induction, which changes voltage and works on AC only.

(3) Because it needs a CHANGING flux to induce anything in the secondary. Direct current gives a steady flux, and a steady flux induces nothing. It is Faraday's law again, and the whole of the last lesson in one sentence.

part: Part F: what it was all for
title: Maxwell's Equations, Waves and the Speed of Light
lead: Everything so far has been building to one result. Two constants measured with magnets and static charge, neither of them anything to do with light, combine to give the speed of light exactly.

blocks.text: The moment two subjects turned out to be one

blocks.label: A number nobody was looking for
blocks.html:
Start with where the two constants came from.

  1. ε0 was measured by experiments on static charge: how strongly two charges pull on each other.
  2. µ0 was measured by experiments on magnets and currents: how strongly two wires push.
  3. Neither experiment involved light in any way. Nobody shone anything at anything.

Maxwell put his four equations together for empty space and found they gave a wave equation. Every wave equation carries a speed, and this one came out as v = 1 / √(µ0ε0) (µ0 = 4π x 10-7 H/m, ε0 = 8.85 x 10-12 F/m, v in metres per second).

Then he put the numbers in.

Multiply
µ0ε0 = 4π x 10-7 x 8.85 x 10-12
= 1.113 x 10-17
Square root
√(1.113 x 10-17) = 3.336 x 10-9
Invert
v = 1 / 3.336 x 10-9
Answer
v = 2.998 x 108 m/s

Key point

2.998 x 108 m/s is the measured speed of light. Not close to it. It. Two laboratory constants about charge and magnetism had the speed of light hidden inside them all along.

Maxwell wrote that we can scarcely avoid the inference that light consists in the transverse undulations of the same medium which is the cause of electric and magnetic phenomena. He predicted electromagnetic waves from pure mathematics, never saw one, and never built an antenna. Hertz confirmed them in 1887, eight years after Maxwell died.

Say it bluntly

Light IS an electromagnetic wave. Optics and electricity are the same subject.

blocks.label: The wave relations
blocks.html:
QuantityFormulaNote
Speedc = 1/√(µ0ε0)2.998 x 108 m/s
Fields linkedE = cBAt every point, every instant
Wave relationc = fλSame c for all of the spectrum
IntensityI = ½ε0cE02Watts per square metre
Poynting vectorS = (1/µ0)E x BEnergy flow per unit area

What every letter means

SymbolMeaningUnit
cSpeed of the wave in vacuumm/s
E0, B0AMPLITUDES, the peak values, not the instantaneous onesV/m and T
f, λFrequency and wavelengthHz and m
IIntensity, the average power crossing unit areaW/m2
SPoynting vector, instantaneous energy fluxW/m2
The Poynting vector, and its useful name

S = (1/µ0) E x B gives the rate at which energy is transported per unit area.

The name is a happy accident: the vector POINTS the way the energy travels, which is the direction of E cross B, at right angles to both fields. Average it over a cycle and you get exactly the intensity I.

Two more forms of the intensity, all equal, and a question may hand you B rather than E: I = E02/(2µ0c) = cB02/(2µ0). Choose whichever matches the amplitude you were given.

E = cB is why B always looks tiny. Dividing by 3 x 108 shrinks the number by eight orders of magnitude, which is why radio engineers quote E and not B.

blocks.label: The plane wave, symbol by symbol
blocks.tag: the formula that looks worse than it is
blocks.html:
The wave itself is written down like this, and it looks far worse than it is.

Ey = E0 sin(kx - ωt)  and  Bz = B0 sin(kx - ωt)

Take it apart one symbol at a time.

SymbolMeaningUnit
EyThe electric field, and the subscript says it points along yV/m
BzThe magnetic field, pointing along z, at right angles to Etesla, T
E0, B0The AMPLITUDES, the peak values each one reachesV/m and T
kWave number, k = 2π/λ. How much phase per metre of spaceper metre, m-1
ωAngular frequency, ω = 2πf. How much phase per second of timeradians per second
xPosition along the direction the wave TRAVELSmetre, m
tTimesecond, s
k and omega are the same idea twice

k packs 2π into one wavelength of SPACE. k = 2π/λ
ω packs 2π into one period of TIME. ω = 2πf

One wave, measured two ways: how it repeats as you move along it, and how it repeats as you wait. Divide one by the other and you get back the speed: ω/k = 2πf/(2π/λ) = fλ = c.

Three directions, all at right angles. E along y, B along z, and the wave travelling along x. Hold your thumb and two fingers out at right angles to each other and you have the picture: no two of them ever lie along the same line.

Both fields share the identical sin(kx - ωt). That is not decoration. It means E and B peak together and vanish together, perfectly in step. It is why E = cB holds at every instant and not just on average.

Your turn. A wave has λ = 2 m and f = 1.5 x 108 Hz. Find k and ω, and check the speed.

Wave number
k = 2π/λ = 2π/2 = π per metre

Angular frequency
ω = 2πf = 2π x 1.5 x 108
ω = 9.42 x 108 rad/s

Check the speed
ω/k = 9.42 x 108 / π
= 3.0 x 108 m/s

The speed of light, as it had to be.

blocks.label: Energy density: the two halves are equal
blocks.html:
A wave carries energy in BOTH of its fields, and the total energy per cubic metre is:

u = ½ε0E2 + B2/(2µ0) (u the energy density in joules per cubic metre, E and B the instantaneous field values)

Two terms: the first is the energy in the electric field, the second the energy in the magnetic field.

Key point, and it is the thing to remember

Because E = cB and c = 1/√(µ0ε0), those two terms are exactly equal.

The wave carries half its energy electrically and half magnetically, always, everywhere. So you can compute one half and double it.

Notice the family resemblance to two formulas you already know: ½CV2 for a capacitor's electric field and ½LI2 for an inductor's magnetic field. The same two halves, the same squares, and here they simply travel.

Your turn. A wave's electric energy density at some instant is 4 x 10-6 J/m3. What is the total?

The two halves are equal
electric: 4 x 10-6
magnetic: 4 x 10-6
Total
u = 8 x 10-6 J/m3

Just double it. You never needed E, B, ε0 or µ0 at all.

blocks.label: The laser pointer, worked in full
blocks.tag: two steps, and a square root
blocks.problem: A laser pointer emits 5.0 mW of power in a beam with cross-sectional area 3.0 x 10<sup>-6</sup> m<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the intensity, and the electric field amplitude.
blocks.working:
Step 1. Convert
5.0 mW = 5.0 x 10-3 W
A = 3.0 x 10-6 m2

Step 2. Intensity is power per unit area
I = P/A
I = 5.0 x 10-3 / 3.0 x 10-6
  = 1667 W/m2

Step 3. Rearrange for the amplitude BEFORE substituting
I = ½ε0cE02
E02 = 2I / (ε0c)
E0 = √(2I / ε0c)

Step 4. Top and bottom separately
top: 2 x 1667 = 3334
bottom: 8.85 x 10-12 x 3.00 x 108 = 2.655 x 10-3

Step 5. Divide, then take the root
3334 / 2.655 x 10-3 = 1.256 x 106
E0 = √(1.256 x 106)
  ≈ 1120 V/m

Why the answer is alarming

1667 W/m2 beats full sunlight, which is about 1000 W/m2, from a pointer drawing only 5 milliwatts. Nothing is powerful here. The energy is simply squeezed into a few square micrometres, and that is exactly why a laser pointer can damage an eye and a 5 mW lamp cannot.
blocks.answer: I = 1667 W/m<sup>2</sup>, and E<sub>0</sub> ≈ 1120 V/m
blocks.redo: Redo it with the beam widened to 3.0 x 10<sup>-5</sup> m<sup>2</sup>, ten times the area. The intensity falls by ten to 167 W/m<sup>2</sup>, but the amplitude falls only by √10, to about 354 V/m, because E<sub>0</sub> is squared in the intensity. Spreading a beam weakens the field more slowly than it weakens the intensity.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.question:
(1) A radio transmitter produces an electromagnetic wave with an electric field amplitude of 0.080 V/m. What is the corresponding magnetic field amplitude?

(2) You double the electric field amplitude of a wave. What happens to its intensity?

(3) What does the Poynting vector give you, and which way does it point?
blocks.answer:
(1) Given
E0 = 0.080 V/m
c = 3.0 x 108 m/s

Formula
E = cB, so B = E/c

Substitute
B0 = 0.080 / 3.0 x 108

Answer
B0 = 2.67 x 10-10 T

Check
Tiny, as it must be: dividing by the speed of light shrinks it by eight orders of magnitude. An answer LARGER than 0.080 would mean you multiplied instead of dividing, which is the commonest slip here.

(2) It QUADRUPLES. I = ½ε0cE02, and the field is squared, so twice the field is four times the intensity.

(3) The rate at which energy is transported per unit area, in W/m2. It points along E cross B, which is the direction the wave travels, at right angles to both fields.

blocks.sub: And E = cB is why the magnetic part always looks so small.
